CHAPTER VII.
A Mad Tea-Party


At a table set under a tree, the March Hare, the Hatter, and a
sleepy Dormouse were having tea. They insisted there was "no room"
for Alice, though the table was mostly empty. The Hatter asked his
famous riddle about a raven and a writing-desk, then explained that
he had quarreled with Time itself, so it was always six o'clock, tea
time, at his table.

The Dormouse began a story about three sisters living at the bottom
of a treacle-well, constantly interrupted by the Hatter and March
Hare. Offended by their rudeness, Alice left and wandered back
through the wood, finding a door in a tree that led back to the long
hall with the glass table, allowing her to finally enter the garden.
